symptoms: Discoloration and rotting of the central spear leaf
Spear leaf turns pale yellow, withers, and dries up
Foul odor emanating from the infected central spindle tissue
Spear leaf easily pulls out from the crown upon gentle tugging
Progressive collapse of young surrounding fronds
causes: High relative humidity (>90%) and continuous rainfall during monsoon
Waterlogging around coconut palm root zone
prevention: 1. Provide proper field drainage to prevent water stagnation
2. Maintain adequate spacing (7.5m x 7.5m) between palms
3. Perform pre-monsoon prophylactic spray of 1% Bordeaux mixture on palm crown
control_measures: 1. Remove infected spindle leaves and clean affected crown tissue
2. Apply 1% Bordeaux paste to cleaned crown area
3. Protect cleaned crown with polythene cover during rain
4. Apply recommended bio-fungicide Trichoderma viride paste for early infections
cultural_practices: Clean palm crowns annually before southwest monsoon onset
Remove and burn dead trees to eliminate inoculum source
water_management: Ensure proper drainage channels in coconut gardens during heavy monsoons
Avoid drip or overhead irrigation hitting palm crowns
nutrient_management: Apply recommended NPK (500g N, 320g P2O5, 1200g K2O per palm/year)
Apply 50kg organic manure or compost per palm annually
severity_indicators: Moderate: Spear leaf rotting with foul smell
Severe: Crown collapse and tree mortality
source: Coconut Development Board (CDB), Government of India
Kerala Agricultural University (KAU) Adhoc Package of Practices for Coconut

symptoms: Dark brown necrotic lesions on distal leaflets of young fronds
Affected leaflets dry up, shrivel, and tear into ragged fan-like shapes
Sunken necrotic spots along leaflet margins
Foliage appears burnt or shredded in upper crown
causes: Secondary fungal infection (Bipolaris halodes, Colletotrichum gloeosporioides) following Rhynchophorus or Phytophthora damage
Prolonged humid weather and high rainfall
prevention: 1. Regular crown sanitation and removal of rotten leaflet parts
2. Apply prophylactic crown treatment before monsoon season
control_measures: 1. Cut away severely affected rot-damaged leaf tips and burn them
2. Spray 1% Bordeaux mixture or 0.2% Mancozeb on affected central leaves
3. Apply bio-control agent Pseudomonas fluorescens (50g in 500ml water) into leaf axils
cultural_practices: Remove rotten leaflets during regular palm maintenance
Maintain optimal plant health through balanced fertilization
water_management: Maintain consistent root zone soil moisture without waterlogging
nutrient_management: Apply 1kg Magnesium Sulphate per palm annually for leaf health
Ensure adequate Potassium supply to improve disease tolerance
severity_indicators: Moderate: Shredded leaflets on multiple upper fronds
Severe: Extensive leaf area destruction across crown
source: ICAR - Central Plantation Crops Research Institute (CPCRI), Kasaragod
Kerala Agricultural University (KAU) Plant Pathology Advisory

symptoms: Yellowish-brown spots on older fronds that turn gray with dark brown borders
Minute black fruiting bodies (acervuli) visible on gray spots
Premature drying and blighting of outer leaf fronds
causes: Potash deficiency in soil predisposes palms to infection
prevention: 2. Prune heavily infected lower leaves and destroy them
control_measures: 2. Spray 1% Bordeaux mixture or 0.25% Copper Oxychloride on foliage
cultural_practices: Keep coconut basin clean and free of weed competition
water_management: Irrigate during dry summer months (45-50 liters/palm/day)
nutrient_management: Apply additional 500g Muriate of Potash (MOP) per palm in deficient soils
source: ICAR - CPCRI Kasaragod Coconut Disease Management Guide
Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU) Agritech Portal

symptoms: Exudation of dark reddish-brown liquid from bark cracks on stem base
Exuded fluid dries into black sticky patches
Internal fibrous stem tissues decay into dark spongy mass
Crown foliage turns yellow and nut yield drops significantly
causes: Fungal pathogen Thielaviopsis paradoxa entering through stem wounds or growth cracks
Soil moisture fluctuations and heavy soil texture
prevention: 1. Avoid mechanical damage or wounds to coconut stem during weeding/harvest
2. Maintain organic mulching around coconut basin
control_measures: 1. Chisel out infected diseased bark tissue cleanly
2. Apply Coal Tar or 5% Calixin/Bordeaux paste to chiseled stem area
3. Root feed with 2% Carbendazim (100ml water) twice a year
cultural_practices: Apply neem cake (5kg/palm/year) in soil basin
water_management: Avoid waterlogging at stem base during rainy season
severity_indicators: Mild: Single bleeding spot on lower trunk
Severe: Multiple bleeding lesions extending up stem
source: Coconut Development Board (CDB) Disease Management Bulletin
ICAR - CPCRI Stem Bleeding Extension Leaflet

symptoms: Premature shedding of buttons and immature nuts
Decay of root tips and reduced absorption
Inflorescence drying and yellow frond tips
causes: Severe soil moisture stress or sudden waterlogging
prevention: 1. Maintain regular summer irrigation and winter basin mulching
2. Apply Borax (50g/palm/year) to prevent button shedding
control_measures: 1. Apply 50g Borax in basin along with organic manure
2. Ensure proper soil drainage and apply Trichoderma enriched compost
cultural_practices: Mulch basin with green leaves or coconut husk
source: TNAU Agritech Portal Coconut Production Guide
KAU Package of Practices for Crops
